adversarial.claim: stamping --args on the template is enough for Factory executes after merge
adversarial.finding: Factory executeJob POSTs overrides.containerOverrides[{args}] and executeJobViaGcloud uses --args=${args.join(",")}. Those REPLACE template args. writerArgs() in bexar-cad.mjs returns only --county, optional --limit/--apply/--run-id. It does not include --writer. A Factory-driven execute after this merge still fails WRITER_REQUIRED unless Factory is updated. This card cannot touch hauska-factory. Template stamp still required: A-019, execute without overrides uses the template, merge-without-yaml is an outage for any path that does not override args.

recommendation.question: Does extending this yaml to well-fact, building-footprint, utility-easement, and setback belong in this PR?
recommendation.answer: Own card. Do not start it in this PR.
recommendation.reasoning: This gap is an outage of the one existing CAD job. The allowlist unlocks four writers in the entrypoint and is still false operationally. well-fact and footprint already have a P4 leftover (factory-atoms-wells / factory-atoms-footprint). Setback --apply is held. Each writer is a different (entity_type, county_fips) lease scope and needs its own job name, timeout, and execute contract. A-019 rebuild re-pins every job named in the config, so five deploys is a real card, not a drive-by. Factory writerArgs must also pass --writer on execute because overrides replace template args; that is a Factory card.
